open_points.subject: read the latest artifact of a type
open_points.text: | read the latest artifact of a type | owner; a service |
open_points.question: May Cabinet Kernel call this for the agent on any project, or only on a project its session is granted? If not granted, what is the refusal, given that R0-47 says no answer may reveal whether a project exists?
options: Kernel for the agent only on a granted project, like list artifacts
Kernel never reads it for the agent
open_points.default_guess: Kernel for the agent only on a project its session is granted; any other project gets the same refusal as the agent projection

open_points.subject: publish / withdraw an artifact pointer
open_points.text: | publish an artifact pointer | producer service; the owner for any owner service |
open_points.question: R0-41 has the agent publish and withdraw Kernel's pointers only on a granted project, but these rows carry no session confinement and no 'not granted' failure. Is Kernel's publish always under agent authority and confined to the session's set, or does Kernel also publish as a plain producer?
options: Kernel publishes only for an agent session, confined to its set
Kernel has both a producer authority and an agent authority
open_points.default_guess: Kernel publishes and withdraws only for an agent session, on a granted project; a project outside the set is refused as not granted

open_points.subject: validate a project reference for the agent
open_points.text: Kernel for the agent on a project its session is granted (R0-46) (R0-41) | exists, active, and why not (`not_found`, `archived`) | —
open_points.question: What does validate answer Kernel for the agent when the project is not in the session's set? It must not reveal whether the project exists (R0-47), and the table says the answer carries every failure.
options: answer not_found for any project outside the set
refuse as not granted, with the same answer whether or not the project exists
open_points.default_guess: one refusal, identical for existing and missing projects, never not_found versus archived

open_points.subject: restricted customer
open_points.text: no new project or correction of a project may name it (R0-37, R0-51)
open_points.question: The create and correct project rows do not list naming a restricted customer as a failure. Does a restricted customer's project stay readable and workable by services and the agent, or does 'ordinary processing stops' affect it?
options: refuse create/correct naming a restricted customer; the project's other operations go on
also limit the project's operations while its customer is restricted
open_points.default_guess: add the refusal to create/correct; the project's other operations continue, since they carry only customer_ref

open_points.subject: end a customer relationship
open_points.text: the Customer marked as ended on that date; its retention period runs from it
open_points.question: After a relationship ends, can it be reopened? Can a new project or correction name the customer? Can the customer still be corrected?
options: final; naming the customer is refused
reversible by recording a new relationship
open_points.default_guess: the end can be undone by the owner while the retention period still runs; naming the customer stays allowed until then

open_points.subject: retention erasure
open_points.text: When the applicable period ends, Registry itself erases or anonymises the data
open_points.question: No row carries the action Registry performs on its own when a period ends. Who triggers it, what does it output (audit entry, notice to the owner), and what is its failure, for example a lawful ground that holds the data back?
options: a scheduled Registry action, audited, with no caller
an owner-confirmed action prompted by Registry
open_points.default_guess: a Registry-initiated action with an audit entry naming Registry as the principal; held-back data is listed for the owner

open_points.subject: owner's view of sessions and requests
open_points.text: the owner sees the registered sessions in the owner interface
open_points.question: No row lists the agent sessions or the pending access requests for the owner. What does that action return, and how are sessions identified to the owner?
options: one 'list agent sessions' row with each session's set, active project and pending request
separate list rows for sessions and for requests
open_points.default_guess: add 'list agent sessions' (owner): each session with its granted set, active project and pending request

open_points.subject: answer an access request
open_points.text: declining changes nothing; the session reads the outcome in its access
open_points.question: A decline leaves the access unchanged, so the session cannot tell a decline from a pending request. Does the session's access read show the request's state?
options: the access read shows the pending request's state: pending, granted or declined
the outcome is not visible to the session
open_points.default_guess: the access read carries the state of the session's last request

open_points.subject: revisions on changes
open_points.text: A change states the revision it was made against; a change against an older revision is refused
open_points.question: R0-35 covers every change, but only 'correct a project' and 'correct a customer' list stale-revision refusal. Do archive, erase, restrict, end relationship, grant, revoke and add room state a revision?
options: every change of a project or customer states a revision
only corrections state one
open_points.default_guess: archive, erase, restrict and end relationship state the record's revision; session access changes use the access version

open_points.subject: import projects with their identity
open_points.text: the projects of the running instances under the identities they carry
open_points.question: Which running instances are the sources, given that R0-50 says test-instance data is never carried over? What happens when two source instances hold the same id (R0-21)? Is there no import at all after this one migration, although R0-34 and R0-44 speak of import as a standing path?
options: name the source instances explicitly; refuse the import on any conflict between sources
allow later imports under the same rules
open_points.default_guess: sources named by the owner in the import; a conflict between sources refuses the whole import; no import after the migration

open_points.subject: agent session identity
open_points.text: Registry checks on every agent-authority call, independently of Kernel, that the project belongs to the session's set
open_points.question: Registry learns which session a call is for only from Kernel, which also registers the sessions. What makes Registry's check independent of Kernel, and does Registry trust Kernel's session claim?
options: Registry trusts Kernel's session claim; independence covers only the set check
the session carries a proof Kernel cannot forge, for example one bound to the owner's grant
open_points.default_guess: state explicitly that Registry trusts Kernel's session naming and checks the set itself

open_points.subject: owner interface reachability from VM Agent
open_points.text: the owner interface, reachable from outside only through the owner's VPN, over HTTPS
open_points.question: Is the owner interface unreachable from VM Agent, as the service API is? Otherwise the agent could reach the owner's sign-in surface.
options: unreachable from VM Agent
reachable but protected only by the owner credential

open_points.subject: R0-37 audit
open_points.text: Every significant operation leaves an audit entry
open_points.question: Which operations are significant? Are reads of personal data, agent-authority calls, refusals, sign-ins and Registry's own retention erasures included?
options: every change plus every personal_data read and every refusal
changes only
open_points.default_guess: every change, every personal_data read, every agent-authority call, sign-ins and retention erasures

open_points.subject: R0-45 standing
open_points.text: the owner's answers of 2026-10-27 on its conflicts with that frame are recorded as R0-24 to R0-52
open_points.question: R0-45 is marked 'proposed to the owner … no objection', not an owner answer. Is it an owner decision like the others, or still open?
options: it counts as an owner decision
it is an open question until the owner confirms it
open_points.default_guess: treat it as decided, and have the owner confirm it explicitly
